title: Recovering a Deleted Branch
description: A feature branch containing unmerged work was accidentally deleted. Recover the commits, verify the recovered history, and safely restore the work to main.

tasks.label: Switch to the recovered branch and verify both original commits
Merge the recovered payment-validation work into main
Delete the recovered branch after the work is safely merged

hints: The branch name is gone, but deleting a branch does not immediately delete the commits it pointed to. Think about where Git records previous reference positions.
Look for the last position of feature/payment-validation. You only need the latest lost commit because its parent contains the earlier payment-validation commit.
Look at Git's record of recent branch and HEAD movements. Find the last commit that belonged to feature/payment-validation, then use that commit to restore the branch.

intro.message: Amit deleted the payment-validation branch before opening the PR. The work was already committed, and the release is getting closer. We need to recover the work without recreating it from scratch.

restoreBranch.message: The branch name is gone, but that doesn't necessarily mean the commits are gone. Think about where Git keeps track of previous reference positions.

verifyRecovery.message: The branch is back. Before we trust the recovery, switch to it and inspect the history. We need to know that both original payment-validation commits survived.

mergeRecovery.message: The original work is safely recovered and verified. Now bring it back into main so the team can continue.

cleanupBranch.message: The recovered work is safely in main. Clean up the temporary recovery branch so the repository is back in good shape.

success.message: Oh thank god. Seriously, thank you — I thought that work was gone for good.

failure.message: The recovery isn't complete yet. Make sure the original branch was recovered, its history was checked, the work was merged into main, and the temporary branch was cleaned up.
